title: Backup and Recovery
description: Protect Git repositories from hardware failure, human error, and accidental data loss with backup strategies and recovery techniques.

data.text: Even though Git is distributed, teams still need centralized backups for hosted repositories. Accidental branch deletion, force pushes, disk corruption, and human error are all common. A solid backup and recovery plan ensures you can restore service and history without panic.

A Git repository is more than the files in `.git/objects`. Backups should include refs, hooks, config, and reflogs. LFS objects, if used, live separately and must be included in the backup plan as well.

items: **Objects and refs** — The core data in `.git/objects` and `.git/refs/`.
**Reflogs** — `.git/logs/` contains reflogs for branches and HEAD.
**LFS objects** — `.git/lfs/objects/` or remote LFS storage must be backed up separately.

data.text: A bare repository contains only the Git data, no working tree. Mirroring a bare repo with `--mirror` copies all refs, including remote-tracking branches and notes. This is the simplest and most reliable backup method.

data.title: Create a mirror backup
data.code:
# Mirror the source repo to a backup location
git clone --mirror https://github.com/example/repo.git backup-mirror.git

# Update the mirror daily
cd backup-mirror.git
git remote update --prune

data.text: Most recovery operations are local. The reflog, `git fsck`, and `git reflog` let you recover from force pushes, rebase conflicts, and corrupted objects without touching a backup. Reserve full restores for hardware failure or server loss.

data.title: Recover a lost branch after a force push
data.code:
# Find the old HEAD in the reflog
git reflog

# Create a recovery branch from the reflog entry
git branch recovery-branch HEAD@{5}

# Verify the commit graph
git log --oneline --graph --all

data.title: Repair a corrupted repository
data.code:
# Verify object connectivity and detect corruption
git fsck --full

# If objects are missing, restore from backup
# Then repack and prune
git repack -a -d --depth=250 --window=250
git prune
git gc

data.title: Backups are useless if untested
data.text: A backup you have never restored is just an assumption. Schedule periodic recovery drills: restore a mirror to a fresh directory and verify that all branches, tags, and recent commits are intact.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Back up the entire `.git` directory or use `git clone --mirror` for reliable copies.
Reflogs and `git fsck` handle most local disasters without a full restore.
Include LFS objects in your backup plan.
Test restores regularly so you know the process works under pressure.
